title: Decide and reconcile the four releases whose stored notes differ from their tag's CHANGELOG section
description:
Found by QCLI-407's reviewer pass on 2026-09-29, and filed rather than folded into that change: it is a decision about existing artefacts, not part of reading new ones.

QCLI-407 re-sourced the GitHub Release notes from the checkout to the commit v<version> peels to, and QCLI-401's existing-release check compares a stored body against those notes. Four live releases were cut or backfilled on 2026-09-27 from a working tree that differed from their tag, so `node scripts/github-release.mjs --version <v>` now REFUSES for them where it previously said "would mark it latest". Measured with the tool's own normaliseNotes semantics -- characters in the tag's section versus characters in the stored body: 0.6.1 5008 vs 500; 0.6.2 5494 vs 10048; 0.7.0 7078 vs 7661; 0.8.0 14631 vs 16812. 0.6.0 differs under the old code too, so it predates the tool and is not evidence either way.

Nothing automated reaches those versions: the flow cuts only the version being promoted, the forward path matches (0.11.0 was checked end to end and matches), and --rollback never touches releases. So this is a repair-path question rather than a release blocker, and it matters the next time a person runs the repair tool for one of those versions.

Why it is not a mechanical fix: for each release, WHICH body is the one to keep is a judgement. 0.6.1's and 0.8.0's stored bodies are later-authored and carry "tagged, never published" in their headings, which the tag's section does not -- so reconciling blindly to the tag would destroy text someone wrote deliberately. The alternative is to leave those releases alone and give the tool an explicit rule for a release that predates QCLI-407.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each of the four releases (0.6.1, 0.6.2, 0.7.0, 0.8.0) has an explicit decision recorded -- keep the stored body, or reconcile it to the tagged section -- with the reason, and the "tagged, never published" question is settled for 0.6.1 and 0.8.0 rather than resolved by default
Whatever the decision, running `node scripts/github-release.mjs --version <v>` for each of the four reports something an operator can act on, and the release runbook's text matches that behaviour
The existing-release comparison carries an explicit, recorded rule for a release cut before QCLI-407, so the next legacy or backfilled release does not resurface this as a fresh finding

plan: 1. Record the ruling on this task: keep the stored bodies for all four (0.6.1, 0.6.2, 0.7.0, 0.8.0), each with its reason; the two never-published ones settled explicitly rather than by default.

2. scripts/github-release.mjs: add a closed, recorded table of the four versions with their reasons. The existing-release comparison REPORTS a recorded exception by name and reason for those four instead of the notes-differ refusal; no release body is edited, and every other version keeps the current verdicts.
3. Test: each of the four reports its recorded exception and reason, a version not in the table still refuses on differing notes, and a matching body is unchanged.
4. Update the release runbook text (lore sync then lore check) so it matches the tool behaviour for the four.
5. bun run check exits 0, reviewer pass over the scripts change, land via a branch and PR into dev.
implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED AND LANDED, 2026-09-29, as 9053905d (PR opum-ai/quest-cli#410, squash into dev).

RULING. opum-agent ruled OPTION A on 2026-09-29 after the A/B packet: each release KEEPS its stored body, and the tool carries a recorded, closed table of the affected versions, each with its reason, reporting them by name rather than refusing or exempting silently. No release body is edited. The ground is the fleet's retirement-scope rule -- history is left alone because rewriting it falsifies it.

DECISIONS RECORDED, one per release, each with its reason; all five verified against the live bodies by ref:
- 0.6.0 -- KEEP. Its stored body is an out-of-band provenance record that exists nowhere in CHANGELOG.md: the tag peels to a9fbc78 (the post-recreation initial commit) while npm's gitHead for 0.6.0 is ce551cf4, which does not exist here; the body advises citing the npm version over the tag. FOUND BY MEASUREMENT AFTER THE RULING and added by a second ruling the same day -- the task description's "0.6.0 differs under the old code too, so it predates the tool and is not evidence either way" is a statement about the QCLI-407 finding, NOT an exclusion from the class, and must not be read as one.
- 0.6.1 -- KEEP. Tagged at 1fa0fef and never published (every attempt hit a registry E404 before writing anything); the body REPLACES the section with that note; the content shipped as 0.6.2; the tag is not re-pointed because quest-web's CI cites this repository's tags. The "tagged, never published" question is settled HERE: the annotation stays, as the body's own record.
- 0.6.2 -- KEEP. Published after its tag; the body is purely additive: the README-in-tarball entry, the release.yml registry-verification fix (QCLI-247), four more Fixed bullets (QCLI-257, 261, 269, 270, 282), and a Known limitations section (missing provenance attestation).
- 0.7.0 -- KEEP. Published after its tag; exactly one added block: the post-release observation that opum-cli-e2e's qualification matrix pinned the literal "Blocked" while a live-reading suite absorbed the same release unmoved.
- 0.8.0 -- KEEP. Frozen, tagged, never published (its content shipped as 0.9.0); the body rewrites its opening and adds two blocks: the never-published annotation with the QCLI-345 correction, and the note on what the removal short-circuit does not cover (LCLI-522). The "tagged, never published" question is settled the same way as 0.6.1: the annotation stays.

WHAT SHIPPED. scripts/github-release.mjs gains a closed RECORDED_LEGACY_NOTES map read through recordedLegacyReason() and recordedLegacyVersions(); the mismatch branch returns {ok: true, action: "recorded-exception"} naming the version's reason, and returns BEFORE any latest handling, so nothing is edited and no recorded version is marked latest. Every other release keeps the notes-differ refusal. scripts/github-release.d.mts carries the new action and both accessors. The module header and the ensureGitHubRelease docblock state the exception, and the docblock records the measured limit: a body reconciled exactly to the tagged section deliberately stops being a recorded exception and is treated as matching -- the one edit the table cannot report. The runbook's operator-facing paragraph states the decision, the split between the four backfilled on 2026-09-27 and 0.6.0 (which always differed), and the tool behaviour; its rollback sentence carries the same qualifier.

EVIDENCE, measured here. End to end: node scripts/github-release.mjs --version <v> exits 0 for all five, naming the version and its reason; 0.11.0 still answers "would mark it latest". test/qcli410-recorded-legacy-notes.test.ts, 4 tests: all five reported with their own reasons under dryRun false, so the no-mutation claim can fail (dry run would entail it); the recorded set asserted BOTH WAYS against the table's own keys; unrecorded versions still refused; a matching body unchanged. THREE MUTANTS each fail the file -- mutating only when !dryRun (which would have survived the first draft), one shared reason across entries, and a table entry added without the test list. Against the pre-change module (3c5d5f06) the file fails on a verdict and on assertions, not at import.

REVIEW. One independent reviewer, two passes. Pass one found the two vacuous assertions above and three precision defects in the prose; pass two re-ran the mutants, confirmed the fixes, and found three one-sentence defects (the limitation sentence was false in the reconciled direction; the set-equality comment was half true; the runbook folded 0.6.0 into a causal class it does not belong to). All fixed. It cleared: ok:true leaking into a wrong action (nothing switches on .action; promote reads only .ok/detail and cannot reach these versions), the never-mark-latest behaviour, the .d.mts union, and the draft/prerelease ordering.

LOCAL ENVIRONMENT, named so it is not read as a verdict on the change: bun run check could not complete on this machine -- the data volume sat at 100%, 205-343MiB free, and test/scale/projection.test.ts dies with SQLITE_FULL writing its projection database. The same suite was green on the pre-delta tree (985 pass / 0 fail), and CI's source-gates ran the full suite green on the PR head cb67a4b1.
finalSummary:
The five GitHub Releases whose stored bodies differ from the section at the commit their tag peels to -- 0.6.0, 0.6.1, 0.6.2, 0.7.0, 0.8.0 -- keep those bodies by recorded decision, and scripts/github-release.mjs reports each by name and reason instead of prescribing a repair that would delete later-authored text.

WHY: QCLI-407 re-sourced the release notes from the checkout to the tagged commit, which moved what the existing-release comparison compares. Four of the 2026-09-27 backfill stopped matching; 0.6.0, whose stored body is an out-of-band provenance record, differs under both comparisons. Each difference is a record written after its tag -- publish histories, a post-release correction, known limitations, a provenance warning -- and rewriting a body to match an earlier section would falsify it.

WHAT CHANGED: a closed table in scripts/github-release.mjs, read through recordedLegacyReason()/recordedLegacyVersions(), and the new recorded-exception verdict -- ok, no edit, never marked latest, because moving the Latest badge onto a version from another era is not a repair. Every other release keeps the notes-differ refusal. The .d.mts contract, the module header, the ensureGitHubRelease docblock (including the measured limit: a body reconciled exactly to the tagged section is treated as matching, the one edit the table cannot report) and the runbook's operator-facing paragraph all state it.

VERIFIED: the tool exits 0 for all five, naming each version's reason, end to end against the live releases, and 0.11.0 still answers "would mark it latest"; 4 tests assert the five, their distinct reasons, the closed set in BOTH directions, the unrecorded refusal and the matching-body path; three mutants fail the file (mutating only when not a dry run, one shared reason, an unlisted table entry) and the pre-change module fails it on verdicts and assertions rather than at import. Two independent reviewer passes; every finding fixed, including one vacuous assertion per pass. typecheck, lint, format:check and layer:check clean; lore check exit 0; CI source-gates green on the PR head. The local full-suite run was blocked by a full disk volume (SQLITE_FULL in the scale suite, unrelated to this change; the same suite was green pre-delta).

LANDED: PR opum-ai/quest-cli#410 squash-merged to dev as 9053905d; this record's closure follows in a chore PR.
